text:
Lena M: Dropping a short design review for the model catalog compare. Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/NEW. Goals: make compare density discoverable, clarify what the perf badges actually measure, and make version-locking/release-narrowing explicit. Also check mobile collapse and keyboard-only flows.

Harper J: I sketched a new compactness slider in the header (0-100) that maps to three breakpoints we ship: Comfortable, Dense, Ultra. Users can drag for immediate feedback. This avoids binary toggles and helps with discoverability. UX question: should we persist the slider per-user or per-org?

Kai W: Implementation notes: sliders are easy for the client but we should map slider positions to CSS token sets and avoid re-creating the DOM. Use CSS classes for the three states and live-preview with a short debounce. Persisting: prefer per-user (localStorage + user setting) so it doesn't surprise other teammates. Also adding a rollback keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+Z) for quick undo of dense changes could be handy.

Maya K: Research says sliders imply continuous control; most users pick presets. Let's show tick marks at the three presets and a tooltip that labels them. Default to Comfortable. Persist per-user makes sense.

Harper J: Badges: users keep conflating "performance" with answer quality. My proposal: surface compact badges with a tiny sparkline icon + numeric p90 and an info chevron. The tooltip shows p50/p90/est cost. Visual variants: pill (label + number) or circular badge (icon + number). Which reads better on narrow columns?

Kai W: Prefer pill for narrow columns because it keeps baseline height consistent. For the sparkline, render an SVG 16x12 inline to avoid layout jank. Accessibility: make badge a button with `aria-haspopup="true"` and `aria-expanded` on toggle so screen readers get the tooltip context. Also ensure tooltip content uses `role="tooltip"` and `aria-live="polite"` when dynamic.

Lena M: On pinning: current pattern is ambiguous. Proposal: change wording to "Lock version in this comparison" and make scope visible: small subtitle under the lock that says either "Local to this comparison" or "Apply to all comparisons". Default to local. Also add an undo snackbar: "Version locked. Undo" for 6s.

Harper J: Edge case when comparing >4 models: locking a version should pin it visually across the horizontal scroll area. Consider a small lock icon overlay on the model avatar and add a filter to view only locked models.

Kai W: Backend needs: `POST /api/compare/lock` with body {compareId, modelId, scope: 'local'|'global'}. We'll emit events `compare.locked` and `compare.lock_undo`. For undo, we can soft-revert client-side then confirm server-side. Also, add a boolean in the compare response `lockedByUser` to avoid extra roundtrips.

Maya K: Accessibility nits: color contrast for the blue info badge is low at small sizes. Use a darker hex for small text and ensure focus outline is 3px wide. VoiceOver reads the tooltip weirdly; set `aria-describedby` from the trigger to the tooltip content element and prefer `aria-live=assertive` for lock confirmations.

Lena M: Permalinks: encode compare state in a sharable link: `?compare=ids:12,34,56&filters=family:gpt&density=compact&locked=12:local`. That allows teammates to share exact state including locks. Also provide an export snapshot action that saves a JSON of the compare state + metrics and returns a permalink for the snapshot.

Harper J: Mobile UX: slider becomes a segmented control. Badges collapse to single-line chips with a chevron to expand a metric sheet. For locking, use a popover confirmation (not long-press). Popover should announce with `role=dialog`.

Kai W: Telemetry: track `catalog.compare.density_change`, `catalog.compare.lock_click`, `catalog.compare.lock_confirmed`, `catalog.compare.lock_undo`, `catalog.compare.share_permalink`, `catalog.compare.export_snapshot`. Include metadata: densityLevel, compareCount, deviceType, userIdHash.

ops-bot: Feature flag created: `catalog_compare_density_slider_v1` in staging. Use `/ff catalog_compare_density_slider_v1 on` to opt in.

Maya K: Next steps: Harper will refine visuals for slider + badges, Kai will stub the lock endpoint + telemetry, Lena and I will draft exact microcopy for lock states and tooltip text. We'll run an accessibility pass and a 1-week canary behind the feature flag. Sync Monday 10am to review the first PRs. Thanks!
